newsitem.title: USA: US FDA cites Acer unit's quality control.
newsitem.headline: US FDA cites Acer unit's quality control.

text.p: U.S. health officials on Friday made public a "warning letter" to Acer Peripherals Inc. of Taiwan complaining of poor quality control and testing of television monitors it ships to the United States.
The Food and Drug Administration said the firm failed to adequately assure the monitors it makes for personnal computers did not emit prohibited levels of radiation.
It said in the letter that FDA inspectors found "several serious deficiencies" in the firm's quality control and testing program, and gave Acer 15 days to correct them.
Firms that do not meet the quality control and testing standards of the FDA, which under U.S. law regulates radiation emission, face a ban on shipments to the United States.
FDA officials said the firm was not being cited for monitors that emit prohibited levels of radiation but that its systems to monitor radiation output were not adequate.

Lillian Gill, director of compliance in the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, said in the letter to Ray Huang, Acer's products safety manager, that the FDA found the deficiencies in a September 25 inspection.

"Based on their findings," she wrote, "the Center for Devices and Radiological Health believes that the current quality control and testing program at the Taoyuan monitor factory (in Taiwan) is not fully adequate to assure that television products and monitors will comply with Federal performance standards and other applicable regulation."
In Taipei, parent company Acer Inc said earlier Friday it would do whatever was necessary to comply with FDA requests for modifications to monitor testing and related procedures.

"We must emphasise that the U.S. government is not questioning the quality or safety of our products per se, but is concerned with testing and other related procedures," Acer Chairman and Chief Executive Stan Shih said in a statement.

"Once notified of this concern, Acer Peripherals has been aggressively and rapidly moving to solve the issues by updating documentation procedures and testing programmes so as to fully comply with the FDA's requests," he said. "We expect to resolve the case within the specified 15-day period."
Acer Peripherals, a key member of Acer group, is the world's third largest colour monitor maker, with factories in Taiwan, Malaysia and China.

Only its Kweishan plant in Taiwan, which makes some 50,000 monitors per month, was affected by the FDA request, the statement said. The firm's Malaysia's plant can turn out 200,000 monitors per month, it said.
In 1995, Acer group's combined revenues totalled US$5.8 billion.
